scene: A black-haired cartoon man with half-lidded eyes and a small closed-mouth smile sits in a wooden chair at a round table on a beach terrace, holding a white coffee cup in his right hand. The table holds an orange juice glass with a lemon wedge, a croissant plate with orange slices and two strawberries, an empty saucer with a folded napkin, and a black smartphone showing a short green line of text that is not legible. Behind him are a railing, a potted palm, a sandy beach, sea with low sun on the right and green hills at the left.
mechanism: A leisure-lifestyle vignette with no words: breakfast, sea view and a phone with a green readout stand in for income arriving while he relaxes, leaving the dividend idea entirely to the title.
composition: The man occupies the left-centre third with his head in the upper left, and the table with phone and food forms a lower-centre secondary cluster. The horizon sits at about one third from the top, and the right side is open sea and sand, so the frame is balanced but has no single dominant hook element.
typography: There is no text, so the headline burden sits entirely on the title. At 160x90 the phone's green readout, the one potentially informative element, is a few pixels and cannot be read, so the money cue is lost.
colors: A warm palette of sand beige, tan wood and soft sunset peach is cooled by a blue sea and sky. Saturation is moderate and contrast is gentle, and the cream shirt separates only mildly from the cream-toned background.
psychology: His half-lidded eyes, relaxed posture and slight smile are shown while holding a cup; no worry or urgency cue is present, only an unhurried-comfort pose.
partnership: The title promises a number (how much invested) while the thumbnail shows only the lifestyle outcome, so the image adds mood but no figure, and viewers must rely on the title for the actual question. The risk of revealing too much is low because no amount is shown.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: man's oversized head and sleepy eyes first, then the table with food and phone, then the sunset sea, with nothing else competing.
art: Flat cel-shaded cartoon with consistent dark outlines on the man and furniture; the chairs, railing and palm foliage are coherent and show no melted or doubled-object artefacts. The scene is detailed in the background and the figure is medium sized, so at phone size it reads as a pleasant beach cafe rather than finance.
strength: The calm beach-breakfast scene communicates a passive-income lifestyle outcome in one image.
weakness: No visible text or money symbol large enough to survive mobile, so the topic is not identifiable without the title.
bottleneck: Finance relevance depends on a tiny phone readout that vanishes at 160x90.
action: Hypothesis: Add one large cash-flow figure in a bold outlined type band over the empty sea area, or enlarge the phone readout, and compare against the current text-free version.
counterexample: Seq 3 puts a large headline and three price callouts on a similarly lifestyle-led scene, making the money topic readable at once.
hero_object: coffee cup and phone on beach table
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: STOP HUSTLING DO THIS INSTEAD / $15 / $15 / $20 / SPEED: 0 MPH / 10 HABITS / WORKING HARDER = STAYING BROKE!
scene: Under a full-width headline, a sweating cartoon man with dark under-eye marks and an open mouth runs inside a hamster wheel at the left, with three price-tag icons above him (a taxi-style car, a paper bag with a burger, a laptop) and loose green bills flying out to the left. At the centre a standing man in a navy suit and round glasses points one finger and opens the other palm toward the right. A thick red arrow leads to a smiling man seated on tall stacks of banded cash, holding a checklist with four green ticks above a green bar chart with an up arrow.
mechanism: A two-state story (exhausted hustle on a wheel versus calm wealth on cash) with a suited guide in the middle pointing the viewer from one to the other, and the headline spelling out the instruction.
composition: The suited man is the central anchor and the wheel and cash-pile figures fill left and right thirds, so the red arrow reads as a left-to-right path. The headline takes the top fifth with a red underline under DO THIS; the lower third holds a red caption strip. Many small icons make the frame busy.
typography: Seventeen visible words in all: the five-word headline in heavy black and red capitals is readable at 160x90, but the three price tags, SPEED: 0 MPH and the 10 HABITS card are not legible and the red bottom caption is only barely so. The 10 HABITS card repeats the title's number, which the headline does not.
colors: Black headline on white with a red accent for DO THIS INSTEAD, the arrow and the bottom caption; green is reserved for cash and the chart, giving red as the stress colour and green as the reward colour. Saturation is high on the cash stacks.
psychology: The wheel man shows visible sweat drops, dark eye marks and an open mouth, while the cash-pile man shows lowered lids and a small smile; the suited man looks toward the viewer with a flat stare and a pointing hand, adding an authority-adviser cue.
partnership: The headline says what to stop, the title says the replacement is ten boring habits; the checklist labeled 10 HABITS bridges them, so the thumbnail partly answers by showing the destination. Little is withheld, so reveal risk is medium.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: huge headline first, then the suited man's face and pointing hand, then the red arrow to the cash pile, and last the wheel scene with the small caption.
art: Clean vector cartoon with uniform outlines, but the scale of the cash pile versus the seated man is exaggerated by design. Many small details (tags, bills, chart, checklist) compete; the faces stay clear and the arrow and headline survive mobile.
strength: The wheel-versus-cash-pile pairing explains the contrast between effortful hustle and effortless wealth at a glance.
weakness: Over a dozen separate elements, including three price tags, a speed label, a chart and a caption, create clutter that wastes small-text slots.
bottleneck: The tiny icons and captions cannot be read at phone size, so only the headline and arrow carry the story.
action: Hypothesis: Remove the price tags and bottom caption and enlarge the 10 HABITS checklist card, then compare against the current busy version.
counterexample: Seq 8 shows the opposite density: two words, one arrow and one object.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A purple-haired cartoon man with furrowed brows, wide round eyes and a downturned mouth reclines on a wicker lounger holding an orange smartphone in both hands. Behind him is a lit modern two-storey glass house with a blue pool. Three red speech-bubble price tags read $1.6k near the phone, $1.4M over the balcony and $36 beside a burger and a fry box on a small round table.
mechanism: A rhetorical product-and-price set: phone, house and fast food each tied to a number, with the headline commanding the viewer to stop, leaving open which purchase is the mistake.
composition: The man and lounger fill the lower left and the glass house the right, with the burger table as a small lower-centre anchor; the red tags make a loose zigzag that guides the eye across the frame. The headline spans the full top, partly crossing the roofline of the house, and white margins keep it clear.
typography: Three words of black extra-bold capitals span the full width and stay readable at 160x90. The three price tags are legible even in the smaller render, but the headline never says which of the three prices maps to which item, and the title's number ten is absent.
colors: A black headline sits on white and cream, the house glows amber and the pool is saturated cyan, and the red price bubbles supply the only strong accent. Red is confined to the three price callouts.
psychology: His furrowed brows, wide eyes and flat downturned mouth are directed at the phone he is holding; the pose is relaxed but the face is tense, which fits a mildly scolding message.
partnership: The title lists ten items and a year; the thumbnail narrows it to three priced objects and a command, so it adds visual specificity and withholds which item is the real answer. The mapping of prices to objects is ambiguous, which may either invite curiosity or read as noise.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: black STOP BUYING THESE headline first, then the red $1.4M bubble on the house, then the man's tense face and phone, then the burger and $36 tag.
art: Cartoon figure composited over a glossy rendered house with a warm interior glow; the character's shading style differs from the house's soft gradients, giving a mixed-style look, while the burger and fries are crisp. The headline crossing the roofline is the only overlap issue.
strength: Three legible price tags give an immediate gap-of-scale hook ($36 against $1.4M).
weakness: The price tags float without leader lines, so the viewer cannot tell which price belongs to which object.
bottleneck: The headline does not name a category, so the thumbnail's claim stays vague beyond the three prices.
action: Hypothesis: Draw a small pointer from each price bubble to its own object (phone, house, burger) and compare against the current floating tags.
counterexample: Seq 1 shows a similar leisure scene with no text at all, so Seq 3 shows how much a headline plus prices adds.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: At the right a smiling grey-haired older man with a white beard and round glasses, wearing an open coral-pink overshirt over a dark tee, holds a stone-grey bowl in both hands. The bowl holds apple wedges, blueberries, strawberries, raspberries and dark red grapes, so more than one fruit is shown. The black background is split by a faint vertical line behind the man.
mechanism: A fruit-as-fast-detox proposition: a friendly older figure presents a mixed fruit bowl while the headline attributes an overnight kidney-cleansing effect to it.
composition: The left 55% is a four-line stacked headline and the man occupies the right 40% from head to waist, giving a clear text-versus-subject split. The bowl sits at the lower right as the secondary focus, and the black background leaves no clutter.
typography: Five words in four stacked lines of very heavy capitals: yellow for the first two lines, white for KIDNEYS and white on a red bar for OVERNIGHT. All lines survive at 160x90. The text is a stronger claim than the title's 'best fruit to eat before bed' and names no fruit.
colors: Yellow and white type on near-black yields very high contrast; a red bar highlights OVERNIGHT, and the coral shirt and bowl of berries add the only warm mid-tones. The red bar emphasises timing rather than signalling a hazard.
psychology: The man's raised cheeks, open friendly smile, direct gaze and held-out bowl give a warm, welcoming and approachable cue; no distress or alarm is visible.
partnership: The title says doctor, best fruit before bed and healthy kidneys; the thumbnail changes 'healthy' to 'cleanses' and adds 'overnight', escalating to a rapid-effect claim. The bowl holds several fruits so 'this fruit' is unresolved, and nothing on the image shows a medical credential.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow THIS FRUIT / CLEANSES block first, then the white KIDNEYS and red OVERNIGHT bar, then the man's face, then the fruit bowl.
art: Illustrated painterly-sketch portrait with visible hatching on the shirt and face; hands, glasses and fruit are coherent with no distorted fingers. The man is placed against pure black, so edges are clean and mobile survival is strong.
strength: High-contrast stacked headline with a red timing bar reads instantly at phone size.
weakness: Cleanse-overnight wording is an absolute effect claim and the bowl shows five different fruits, so the key noun is unresolved.
bottleneck: The headline promises a fruit but the picture shows a mixed bowl, leaving the central question visually unanswered.
action: Hypothesis: Replace the mixed bowl with a single clearly shown fruit and compare it against the current mixed bowl to test whether specificity improves clarity.
counterexample: Seq 24 uses the same yellow-white-red stacked layout with an older woman, so the pair shows a repeated format; Seq 21 uses a clock instead of a face.
medical_notes: The headline claims a fruit cleanses kidneys overnight, which is stronger than the title wording, and no doctor credential is visible although the title says Doctor Explains.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon man with dark skin, sunglasses and a green-and-white floral short-sleeve shirt lies back in a brown leather recliner strapped to the top of a red-and-grey rocket. Orange-yellow flames and grey smoke clouds spill out of the base on a plain white background. Very small lettering runs down the rocket body and is not legible.
mechanism: A lift-off metaphor: a reclining man on a rocket suggests an effortless early-retirement launch.
composition: The rocket and chair form a vertical central stack with the headline centred above it; there is large white space on both sides and the smoke spreads along the bottom. The figure is small relative to the frame, so the rocket body is the dominant shape.
typography: Three words of black bold capitals sit centred at the top on white, and they are readable at 160x90. The number 30 is the only age cue; the headline does not link to saving too much or Coast FIRE, which the title names.
colors: Mostly white with a small cluster of warm brown, red and orange in the middle; the green shirt is the single cool accent. Saturation is low overall and the subject is separated by white space rather than contrast tricks.
psychology: Sunglasses hide his eyes and the posture is a fully leaned-back recline, giving a relaxed, confident-looking pose; no emotion beyond that is visible.
partnership: The title argues that saving too much is a mistake and mentions Coast FIRE, while the thumbnail makes the bolder claim of retiring at 30; the title's idea is not shown, so the thumbnail escalates and leaves the connection unanswered.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: RETIRE AT 30 first, then the rocket flames and chair, then the sunglasses figure.
art: Simple vector cartoon with consistent outlines, but the native file is only 360x202 so edges soften when enlarged; the tiny printed word on the rocket is unreadable and adds nothing. Mobile survival is good because the layout is sparse.
strength: Sparse white layout lets the rocket-chair metaphor and the three-word headline read in a glance.
weakness: The tiny figure and low-resolution native file give little facial detail and a generic look.
bottleneck: Distinctiveness is limited by a common retire-early visual and a bold claim without a reason shown.
action: Hypothesis: Add a visible link to the title idea, for example a small gauge or coast label on the rocket, and compare against the current blank body.
counterexample: Seq 7 also uses an age number in text but surrounds it with a rich scene, whereas Seq 5 relies on one object.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: ONE GROWS / MUCH FASTER / 180% / 160% / 140% / 120% / 100% / 80% / 60% / 40% / 20% / 0% / -20% / Day Trading / Index Funds
scene: At the left an egg-headed cartoon man with swept brown hair, wide round eyes and an open mouth wears a blue hoodie and points his index finger to the right. At the centre sits a green dollar money bag, and a thick black curved arrow from the headline points down-left to it. At the right a line chart has a y-axis from 180% to -20%, a red line (Day Trading) hovering near 0 to 10% and a green line (Index Funds) climbing to about 160%.
mechanism: A direct verdict: a pointing figure and a chart show one line pulling far ahead of the other, while the headline names a winner without saying which.
composition: The figure fills the left third, the two-line headline sits upper right and the chart fills the lower right, so the layout reads as a clockwise loop. The arrow points to the bag, not to the green line, so the arrow target and the evidence are separate. White space around the chart is clean.
typography: The four-word headline in heavy black capitals reads at 160x90, with FASTER the largest element. The y-axis percentages and the legend are far too small to read at that size; they do not carry the answer, which is shown by the line gap.
colors: Black on white with a green accent on the winning line and bag and red for the losing line; the blue hoodie is the only other saturated block. Red and green are used semantically to mark the weaker and stronger series.
psychology: His wide eyes and open mouth with a pointing arm read as surprise or emphasis and are directed at the chart, serving as a gesture cue.
partnership: The title asks which of day trading and index funds makes more, and the thumbnail answers visually via the diverging lines while hiding the labels; the headline withholds the name, but the green line already shows the result, so the reveal is fairly high.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: ONE GROWS MUCH FASTER headline first, then the green money bag with the arrow, then the diverging green line, and finally the pointing man.
art: Flat cartoon over what looks like a pasted chart image with a crisp grey grid and small axis labels; the chart's rendering style is different from the figure, a mismatch visible in line weight and font. The two elements are not blended, but each is readable on its own.
strength: The diverging green and red lines make the answer instantly visible even without reading labels.
weakness: The legend and axis labels are unreadable at phone size, so the series are identifiable only by colour, and the arrow targets the bag instead of the winning line.
bottleneck: Which line is which is only given by tiny legend text, so the thumbnail reveals the gap without naming the winner.
action: Hypothesis: Move the arrow to the end of the green line and enlarge the Index Funds label, then compare against the current bag-targeted arrow.
counterexample: Seq 8 shows the opposite choice: a minimal two-word headline and no chart, so nothing is revealed before the click.
hero_object: diverging green and red line chart
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A big round-headed cartoon man in a navy baseball cap, with a raised eyebrow and a closed-mouth smile, stands with arms crossed in a navy suit and red tie. Behind him are windows where an orange sunset skyline at the left meets a starry night skyline at the right. Stacks of gold coins fill both sides, cash bundles sit at the lower left, a gold wristwatch rests on a coin pile at the right of centre, a briefcase with cash is at the right, and a phone and a green rising bar chart appear at the bottom right and in the top-right window.
mechanism: A future-self wealth scene for the 40s: gold coins, a watch, a briefcase and a rising chart surround a confident suited man, with a red arrow tying the age label to his head.
composition: The man's head and torso occupy the central third, the label sits top left with a red curved arrow aiming at his face, and gold stacks frame him on both sides. Perspective is symmetrical, and the split sunset/night background adds depth but also many competing details.
typography: Two words, YOUR 40s, in white outlined capitals at the top left stay readable at 160x90, and the lowercase s is small but legible. The label supplies an age that differs from the title's 30s, so the thumbnail adds a decade the title does not state.
colors: A gold-orange left half and a deep navy right half with cyan stars, plus yellow coin highlights, give a saturated complementary scheme; the red arrow and tie are small accents, and the man's navy suit is somewhat close in value to the right-hand sky.
psychology: The raised brow, closed smile, crossed arms and upright stance are visible confidence cues; the gold, watch and chart add status signals.
partnership: The title says starting wealth building in your 30s and the thumbnail shows the 40s outcome, so the image offers a result a decade later; the mismatch between 30s and 40s is unexplained and could blur the starting point, but the outcome promise is clear.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: white YOUR 40s label, then the red arrow, then the man's face, then the gold coin stacks.
art: Consistent flat cartoon with a glossy gradient on the gold and a smooth light glow; the oversized head is consistent across the figure, and the objects are coherent. The background is dense but low-contrast relative to the figure.
strength: A strong wealth tableau with a single label makes the 40s outcome immediate.
weakness: The dense background has many gold items and the title's 30s starting point is absent, so the age story is split.
bottleneck: Too many wealth props compete with the label, and the thumbnail shows the outcome without any visual cue of a starting decade.
action: Hypothesis: Reduce the coin and cash props by about half and add a small 30s starting marker next to YOUR 40s, then compare against the current version.
counterexample: Seq 5 also leads with an age claim but uses a sparse white layout instead of a dense scene.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon man with auburn hair, wide round eyes glancing to the viewer's right, a closed slight smile and a double chin stands in a navy blazer, grey shirt and jeans, holding a green dollar coin low at his left. A black curved arrow from under the headline points down-left to a green piggy bank with a coin dropping into its slot. A cluster of banded green cash stacks sits at the lower right on white.
mechanism: A beginner-first-step cue: a character, a piggy bank and cash, with the arrow telling the viewer where to begin.
composition: The man fills the left third, the two-word headline sits upper right and the arrow runs diagonally down to the piggy bank, with the cash cluster as a lower-right counterweight. White space is plentiful and every element is separated.
typography: Two words in the heaviest black capitals fill the top right and are clear even at 160x90. The text omits the title's $1,000, 2026 and step-by-step terms, so the amount is not shown anywhere.
colors: A black headline sits on white with green used for the piggy bank, the coin and the cash, and a blue blazer plus peach skin as the only other colours. Green is clearly tied to money.
psychology: His wide eyes look off to the side with a neutral closed smile and a slightly tilted head; the expression is mild and the gesture is just holding a coin, so there is no strong emotional cue.
partnership: The title promises a step-by-step first $1,000 in 2026; the thumbnail's START HERE plus a piggy bank echoes the beginner idea but frames it as saving rather than investing and omits the amount, so the title carries the numbers.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: START HERE first, then the black arrow, then the green piggy bank, then the man's face, then the cash stacks.
art: Standard flat cartoon with clean outlines; the same egg-head character style appears in other thumbnails in this set, and no artefacts are visible. The layout is uncluttered and stays crisp at 160x90.
strength: Two words, one arrow and one saving symbol make a very fast, uncluttered scan.
weakness: The character is generic and the piggy bank signals saving rather than investing, so the topic fit is loose.
bottleneck: No specific amount or concrete first action is shown, so the beginner promise stays generic.
action: Hypothesis: Put a $1,000 coin label on the piggy bank in place of the decorative cash stack, and compare against the current unlabelled bank.
counterexample: Seq 2 shows the opposite density with seventeen visible words and many props, while Seq 8 stays minimal.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon man with dark hair, round wide eyes and a small smile lies back on a large heap of green bills, one hand behind his head and the other raising a fan of bills. He wears a pink polo, beige trousers and white shoes. At the base of the heap a white sheet printed PROMO | TIONS is torn down the middle, with cash showing through the tear, and a black curved arrow runs from the headline down-left to the pile.
mechanism: A refusal-pays-off image: the torn PROMOTIONS paper at the base of a money mountain suggests that turning promotions down leaves him richer rather than poorer.
composition: The money pile fills the lower left with the man reclining diagonally on top, and the huge headline sits upper right with a lot of white space below it. The arrow links the headline to the pile, and the torn paper forms a lower-centre label. The mass of bills is the main texture.
typography: Two enormous black words SAY NO dominate the upper right and the torn-paper label is a second, much smaller tier; at 160x90 SAY NO is perfectly legible and PROMO TIONS is readable but small and split in two by the tear. The headline gives the instruction the title only implies.
colors: A pure white backdrop lets the saturated green of the pile pop; the black headline provides maximum contrast, the pink shirt is a soft accent, and the beige trousers nearly match the bills' tints. Green carries the money meaning.
psychology: The man's wide-open eyes, small smile and legs crossed on the pile show a lounging pose with a raised cash fan; no stress cue is visible, which pairs oddly with a refusal message.
partnership: The title asks whether viewers are right to stop chasing promotions, and the thumbnail turns that into an order (SAY NO) and a payoff image; the visual says refusing promotions is financially safe, which is a bolder implied claim than the title.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: SAY NO first, then the arrow down to the torn PROMOTIONS paper, then the man holding cash on the pile.
art: Flat cartoon man pasted over a hand-drawn pile of bills; the pile's outlines are busy but there is no obvious artefact, and the torn paper has believable ragged edges. The split word is the main legibility issue; the large white area keeps it clean.
strength: A sharp two-word command plus a mountain of cash makes the counter-intuitive stance clear.
weakness: The word PROMOTIONS is split by the tear into PROMO and TIONS, and it is much smaller than SAY NO, so the object of the refusal is easy to miss at phone size.
bottleneck: The thing being refused sits at the bottom in small split text, away from the headline.
action: Hypothesis: Keep the tear but add a horizontal label PROMOTIONS above the paper in the same black type as SAY NO, and compare against the split version.
counterexample: Seq 13 uses a similar white-background cartoon-plus-arrow layout but conveys an emotional warning instead of a reward.
hero_object: torn PROMOTIONS sheet on cash pile
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: leafy white trees, hedges, a slatted bench, a lamp post and a bin
mechanism: A labelled incongruity: an officer tagged KGB gently strokes a cat with a SPY tag nearby, hinting that the cat or the whole scene is part of an espionage story.
composition: The officer stands just right of centre as the tallest vertical, the cat on the bench is the lower-centre focus, and the two tags sit at opposite corners of the diagonal bench, forming a rough triangle. The monochrome white surroundings give a lot of negative space and the viewpoint is angled from above.
typography: white on black KGB at the upper right of centre
colors: The all-white environment is broken by three colours only: grey-green coat, orange cat, and a yellow tag, with a black KGB tag adding contrast. Saturation is very low except for the cat, which gets immediate separation.
psychology: The officer's head is bowed toward the cat in a gentle petting gesture, which reads as a calm and almost tender moment against a military uniform; no alarm is visible.
partnership: The title says the most expensive CIA fail in history; the thumbnail shows a KGB-labelled officer and a SPY tag, so it adds an opposing-agency angle and leaves the 'fail' and the cost unseen. The unanswered question is who is spying on whom, and the cost is not hinted.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: black KGB tag first, then the orange cat as the lone saturated object, then the officer's uniform, then the yellow SPY tag.
art: Clay-white 3D render with soft ambient shading and consistent isometric perspective; the bench, trees and figure share lighting and no distorted fingers or objects are visible. The foliage is highly detailed but nearly white, so it recedes.
strength: The white environment makes the orange cat and the two labels pop with only two words.
weakness: The title's CIA and fail promise has no visible counterpart, and the cat's connection to the SPY tag is ambiguous.
bottleneck: The wide white scene has very low saturation, so the only hooks are two small tags and a pet cat.
action: Hypothesis: Add one visible cue of failure or cost, such as a banded cash stack or a cracked briefcase on the bench, and compare against the current version.
counterexample: Seq 2 shows how a dense cartoon scene with many captions fails at small size, whereas Seq 10 stays sparse.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A huge container ship with an orange hull seen from the bow side, stacked high with red, blue, yellow and orange containers, sails across a blue sky. The waterline cuts the frame, and below it the teal underwater view shows the dark lower hull ending in a rounded orange bulbous bow. At the bottom left, white text sits beside a vertical orange bar.
mechanism: A hidden-below-the-surface reveal: a half-above, half-below view shows the ship's scale and its submerged bulb, framing a how-it-works explainer.
composition: The ship runs diagonally from the left edge to the upper right, the waterline splits the frame in the lower third, and the text block takes the lower left over the dark teal water. The orange hull is the dominant mass, and the bulbous bow at lower centre-right is the secondary point.
typography: Four words in two lines of white mixed-case sans text with an orange vertical bar occupy about half the width at the lower left and are legible at 160x90, though smaller and lighter than the all-caps headlines elsewhere. The text states the topic but not the title's hook about 20ft containers and forever-changing shipping.
colors: A strongly complementary scheme: saturated orange hull against deep blue sky and teal water, with multicoloured containers adding variety. White text on dark teal has good contrast and the orange bar echoes the hull.
psychology: No face or figure is shown, so there is no expression cue; the sheer scale of the ship and the cut-away view give a sense of size and curiosity.
partnership: The title says how 20ft containers changed global shipping forever, while the thumbnail reads How Container Shipping Works; it keeps the topic but drops the change-forever angle and the 20ft detail, so the image supplies the scale instead. Little is hidden, so reveal risk is low.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: orange hull first, then the stacked containers, then the white two-line text, then the underwater bulbous bow.
art: The image looks like a photographic-style render with consistent lighting and a realistic waterline; there is no clear artefact, though whether it is a photo or a render cannot be established from the image. Detail in the container stack is dense but the large hull and sky keep it uncluttered at phone size.
strength: A bold orange-and-blue image of a giant ship shows scale instantly and works at 160x90.
weakness: The caption is generic and a how-it-works explainer promise carries no tension or stake.
bottleneck: There is no emotional or consequence hook, only a topic label and a scale visual.
action: Hypothesis: Replace the caption with a concrete claim, such as a container count or cargo-weight figure, and compare against the generic wording.
counterexample: Seq 16 has the same strong colour separation but adds a story question and character emotion.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A stick-figure man with a white round head, black hair, flat brows and eyes glancing to the right swims at the surface of a blue sea with his arms stretched out. He wears a tattered brown animal-skin wrap tied with rope at his waist. Pale ripple lines surround his body, a flat-topped brown headland sits on the right horizon and small clouds dot the pale sky.
mechanism: A question image: a prehistoric-looking stick figure paddling in open water asks whether early humans could swim, with the sideways glance adding humour.
composition: The swimmer sits near the centre of the lower two-thirds, with the headline across the full top. The horizon line passes through his head, and the large empty blue water gives plenty of negative space, so the hierarchy is a simple two-level one.
typography: Three words in a rounded hand-lettered yellow face with a thick black outline span the entire top edge and read clearly at 160x90, including the question mark. The text raises a yes/no question where the title says how they learned.

psychology: The standing man's half-lidded gaze and flat mouth are a deadpan, impassive look, and the reclining figure's closed smile and hand behind his head reads as relaxed; the pair contrasts passivity with ease.

scene: A stick-figure caveman with wild brown hair and a furrowed, side-glancing stare wears a fur cloak and tattered loincloth, holds a flaming torch aloft in one hand and a stone-tipped spear low in the other. composition: The caveman is the left-side anchor with the torch as a bright high point at the centre, and the animal group fills the right third, creating a clear left-versus-right confrontation. The headline runs across the top, and the horizon glow behind the torch adds a focal halo.
typography: Three words in yellow capitals with a dark outline span nearly the full width at the top, and the headline is easily readable at 160x90. The question wording does not mention animals, but the picture supplies them while the title adds the word fear.
colors: A dusky purple-blue sky and grey-brown ground provide a dark base, so the yellow headline and the orange flame pop, and the brown fur colours of the animals sit in the same family as the figure. Colour semantics are modest: warm fire against cool dusk.
psychology: The animals show wide eyes and open mouths, which reads as fright, while the caveman's furrowed brow and level stare reads as steady and confrontational; the visible contrast sets the frightened-versus-fearless story.
partnership: The title asks why animals learned to fear us and the thumbnail frames it as what scared them, with the human with fire and spear as the visible answer, so it supplies a partial answer with a mild reveal. The thumbnail also does not say 'us', so the viewer must infer that humans are the cause.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow WHAT SCARED THEM? first, then the frightened animals at the right, then the caveman's face and torch.
art: A hybrid style with a stick-style man set in a detailed painted background; the animals' faces use the same cartoon eyes as the figure, which keeps the style consistent. The background is rich yet dim and the main shapes stay clear at phone size.
strength: A clear confrontation between one armed figure and many frightened animals tells the story at a glance.
weakness: The picture partly answers the question by showing the human with fire and a spear, and the background is detailed.
bottleneck: The thumbnail already points to a visible threat, so the unresolved question is smaller than the headline suggests.
action: Hypothesis: Remove the torch and spear and show only the animals reacting to something out of frame, then compare against the current armed figure.
counterexample: Seq 11 has a similar strong colour contrast but no figure or story question.

scene: An egg-headed cartoon man with thinning brown hair, raised brows, a sideways glance and a slightly open mouth rests his hand on his chin. composition: The man fills the left quarter at full height, the huge two-word headline spans the top right, and the mansion with car sits in the lower centre as the secondary focus. The arrow links the headline to the house. Generous white space around each element makes the layout simple.
typography: Two words in the heaviest black capitals plus a question mark span about 60% of the width and are legible at 160x90. The headline contains no verb or subject, so who is faking, and the title's coworker framing, is absent from the image.
colors: A white background, black type and a single saturated pair of colours: gold-yellow on the mansion and a red car with a red outline glow. The man's muted grey-brown clothes make a deliberate low-status contrast with the bright property.
psychology: The raised brows, sideways glance, open mouth and chin-rub pose show visible doubt or puzzlement directed at the house, with ragged clothes adding a status-gap cue.
partnership: The title is about how coworkers afford their lifestyle and the ugly truth; the thumbnail turns it into a two-word suspicion and shows the lifestyle objects but not coworkers, so it escalates to an accusation of fakery that the title only hints at. scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: FAKE LIFE? first, then the glowing mansion and red car, then the arrow, then the man's puzzled face.

text: CLEAN 10 KG OF STOOL / BEFORE / AFTER
scene: A yellow banner across the top holds the headline. Below, three panels sit side by side. At the left, a glowing coral 3D model of the large and small intestine on dark blue has a lumpy dark-brown mass filling the lower colon, with a red rounded BEFORE badge beneath it. At the centre, a photographic-style glass of speckled beige smoothie is being poured over a heap of brown seeds and four dried black prunes on a wooden table. At the right, the same intestine model has a smooth empty colon, with a green rounded AFTER badge.
mechanism: A before-and-after gut story with a drink as the intervention: a clogged colon becomes a clean one after a smoothie of seeds and prunes, with the amount stated in kilograms.
composition: The headline band fills the top sixth, and the three panels are almost equal widths, so the centre drink is flanked symmetrically by the two organ models. The glass in the middle is the vertical anchor, and the coral organs are the highest-saturation shapes. The panels use strong dark-blue and wood-tone separation.
typography: Five words of black capitals on a yellow band, plus two small white-on-colour badge words BEFORE and AFTER. All of it remains readable at 160x90, with the banner words the most legible. The headline adds the 10 kg figure that the title does not state, and the title's drink-tonight and by-morning timing is missing.
colors: A saturated yellow banner, coral-pink organs on dark navy, a red badge for before, a green badge for after, and warm wood tones for the centre; red and green are used semantically for the bad and good states, and the red tag, the brown mass and the yellow band signal alarm on the left side.
psychology: No person or face appears; the lumpy brown mass in the left colon and the empty tube at the right carry the cue, which is a visible disgust-to-relief pairing built from organ imagery.
partnership: The title promises flushing years of gut waste by morning; the thumbnail turns that into a specific 10 kg and a before/after pair, and the stated weight is the sort of exaggerated number that goes beyond what the title says. The impacted-colon imagery is a model rather than a medical image and shows no evidence for the quantity.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow CLEAN 10 KG OF STOOL banner first, then the coral intestine at the left with the brown mass, then the glass of smoothie, then the AFTER organ at the right.
art: The side panels are glossy 3D-style organ models with matching lighting, while the centre looks like a photograph of a glass on a table, so the style mixes renders and photography; the centre photo and the dark-blue panels have unlike backgrounds. Nothing is visibly malformed. The hierarchy survives at mobile size.
strength: A symmetrical before, drink, after layout makes the transformation story clear in one look.
weakness: The 10 KG figure and the clogged-colon model are implausible-looking packaging cues that go beyond the title.
bottleneck: The drink in the centre is easy to overlook against two bright organ models, so the intervention is secondary to the shock imagery.
action: Hypothesis: Remove the 10 KG number and the brown mass, then compare it with a neutral before and after pair that keeps the same drink panel.
counterexample: Seq 12 shows the other extreme: one image, one yellow question and no organ imagery.
medical_notes: The thumbnail states an exact 10 kg stool figure and pairs a clogged-colon model with a drink, which presents an overnight cleanse as a verified outcome without any visible support.

composition: The adult and baby form a lower-left cluster, the lion occupies the right half, and the yellow label with its arrow sits at the top centre; the eye path runs from baby to lion in a diagonal. The picture is dark and heavy with grass and trees, with the pale burst lines and the lion's light mane as the brightest areas.
typography: Three words in thin yellow capitals at the top centre cover about a quarter of the width and are the weakest point; at 160x90 they are readable only with effort. The native image is also only 360x202 pixels, so the small text softens. The label adds a time-span (all night) that the title lacks.
colors: A dark blue-green and olive night palette with warm tan fur and mane, a pale moon glow and yellow label text; contrast is low overall, with the white sound-burst lines and the yellow text as the highest-contrast spots.
psychology: The caregiver's wide eyes and open frowning mouth, the baby's open mouth and the lion's lowered head together show visible alarm, tension and a stalking posture.
partnership: The title asks what ancient humans did when a baby would not stop crying; the thumbnail answers with a visible peril, the lion, and suggests that crying attracts predators, so it escalates the question into a threat while leaving the solution unseen.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: white burst lines around the crying baby first, then the lion on the right, then the caregiver's wide eyes, then the yellow CRYING ALL NIGHT label.
art: Illustrated stick-style figures over a painted night background with consistent outlines; the lion is detailed and coherent and the style matches the characters. The scene is dim and busy with grass, and the low native resolution softens edges.
strength: The lion looming toward a crying baby tells a clear stakes story in one picture.
weakness: The thin yellow label is small and low-contrast at phone size, and the dark scene has little brightness.
bottleneck: Text legibility is the weak link, because the key label is thin and small while the picture is dim.
action: Hypothesis: Thicken the label to an outlined heavy face about twice the current size and brighten the background around it, and compare against the current thin version.
counterexample: Seq 12 uses the same cartoon-ancient setting but makes a bold yellow outlined headline fully readable.

scene: Two orange-skinned cartoon bodies with featureless oval heads, two white oval eyes and a small white dumbbell icon on the forehead stand shirtless in teal drawstring shorts. composition: The two bodies are symmetrical, each filling roughly a third of the width with heads cropped at the top edge, and the headline plus red arrow sits in the narrow white gap between them. The strong orange shapes dominate, and the white centre keeps the text isolated.
typography: Two words in black bold capitals sit at the middle top between the figures and are readable at 160x90, but they are the smallest large element and the pair of bodies overpower them. The text says nothing about habits, belly fat or the title's four-habit list.
colors: Saturated orange bodies and teal shorts are a near-complementary pair on a white background; the thin red arrow is the only line accent. Orange here is the figure's skin colour and does not signal danger, and the dumbbell icon is the single white detail on each head.
psychology: Both figures have blank oval eyes and no mouth, so no emotion is shown; the difference is in body shape and the pinching versus pointing gestures.
partnership: The title promises four boring habits that quietly burn belly fat fast; the thumbnail shows the fat-loss result and the words TOO EASY, which adds an effortlessness claim and hides the habits. The viewer can infer the outcome but not the method.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: orange muscular figure at the right first, then the soft-bellied figure at the left, then the TOO EASY text and arrow.
art: Smooth vector rendering with clean outlines and glossy highlights; both bodies share lighting and proportions, so the pair reads as a consistent character. The identical blank face makes it generic, and the arms and hands are coherent.
strength: Mirrored same-character before and after makes the transformation claim understandable without words.
weakness: The faceless character carries no emotion and the title's four habits are not hinted at.
bottleneck: The thumbnail shows only the result, so the intriguing method (boring habits) never appears in the picture.

counterexample: Seq 18 also uses a before/after pair but labels each state with a colour-coded badge, which Seq 20 does not.

text: NEVER TAKE / BP PILLS / AT THIS TIME / STOP NOW
scene: On a black background four stacked lines of headline run down the left. At the middle top an amber pill bottle with a white blank label and a red stripe sits beside two white round tablets, with a small red-rimmed analog clock behind it. On the right a large red neon-outlined clock with numerals 12, 3, 6 and 9 fills a diagonal red panel, with a red heartbeat line and a grid floor along the bottom and two outlined plus-sign icons at the top and bottom right.
mechanism: A medication-timing alarm: a pill bottle, two clocks and a pulse line combine with an imperative to stop to imply that taking blood-pressure pills at a certain hour is dangerous.
composition: The headline column takes the left 55% in descending size, the pill bottle sits at the centre as the bridge, and the glowing clock fills the right side. The diagonal panel edge pushes the eye from text to clock, and the right half is symmetrical and dense with glow effects.
typography: Nine words in four lines: yellow NEVER TAKE, white BP PILLS, black on a yellow highlight AT THIS TIME and white on a red box STOP NOW. All four lines survive at 160x90, though the pill bottle and the small clock are only shapes. The text leaves the hour unstated, which the clock does not specify either.
colors: A black, red and yellow scheme dominated by the glowing red clock; red and yellow-on-black signal danger and urgency throughout, with white text for the key noun. The amber bottle is the only warm natural colour and the contrast is very high.
psychology: No person is shown, so there is no expression; the clock, red glow, pulse line and the STOP NOW command carry a strong fear and urgency cue.
partnership: The title says the most dangerous time to take blood-pressure medication, while the thumbnail upgrades to the imperative never take at this time and stop now; this is more absolute than the title and the clock never shows which hour is meant, leaving the timing unanswered.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow NEVER TAKE and white BP PILLS first, then the glowing red clock on the right, then the red STOP NOW box, then the pill bottle.
art: A polished digital illustration with glow effects and a perspective grid; the pill bottle has a blank label and the two clocks differ in time and style but are internally consistent. The panel is dense with effects, though the main text stands out on black.
strength: A black, red and yellow alarm scheme and a clock make the urgency read instantly.
weakness: The imperative to stop medication plus an unspecified hour is a stronger and vaguer instruction than the title.
bottleneck: Both clocks show different times and no hour is highlighted, so the key information, the time, is unresolved.
action: Hypothesis: Mark one specific hour on the large clock with a highlight sector, and compare against the unmarked dial.
counterexample: Seq 22 shows the calm opposite: no alarm colours and a relaxed seated figure.
hero_object: red neon clock with pill bottle
medical_notes: The thumbnail tells viewers to never take blood-pressure pills at an unspecified time and to stop now, which could be read as a medication-stopping instruction.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: DRINK WATER / THIS WAY / SAY GOODBYE / TO DIABETES
scene: On a black background an older woman with short grey hair and round glasses, in a teal knit sweater over a patterned collar, holds a clear glass of water to her lips with both hands and has a gentle closed-lip smile with her eyes turned to the left. A four-line headline fills the left: yellow DRINK WATER and THIS WAY, white SAY GOODBYE, and white TO DIABETES on a red box.
mechanism: A drink-water-to-end-diabetes claim: a smiling older woman sips a glass of water beside a headline that says to say goodbye to the disease.
composition: The text block occupies the left 60%, with the woman from head to chest at the right 40% and the glass in the centre-right as the hero. The red box anchors the bottom left. Black background and uniform margins leave no clutter, giving a clear text-versus-portrait split.
typography: Eight words in four lines of heavy capitals read clearly at 160x90, with the yellow top two lines the loudest and the red-boxed TO DIABETES the fourth read. The thumbnail names the disease and an eliminate-it outcome, while the title says support blood sugar and diabetes health, so the headline is a stronger claim than the title wording.
colors: Yellow and white type on black gives very high contrast, the red box with white text highlights the condition, and the teal sweater and pale skin are the only other colours. The red box emphasises the disease name rather than showing a hazard graphic.
psychology: Her closed smile, relaxed shoulders and sideways gaze at the glass are calm and reassuring cues; the sip pose is the only action.
partnership: The title says how seniors should drink water to support blood sugar, with a doctor explaining, while the thumbnail says say goodbye to diabetes, an elimination claim that goes past supporting blood sugar. No doctor credential is visible, so the authority named in the title is not shown.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow DRINK WATER THIS WAY block first, then the red TO DIABETES box, then the woman's face and the glass.
art: Painterly illustrated portrait with soft hatching on the sweater and face; the glass, hands and glasses look coherent, with no visible distortion. The black ground makes the figure and text separate cleanly at mobile size.
strength: A high-contrast stacked headline with a sipping portrait makes the water-and-diabetes message instantly clear.
weakness: The say-goodbye-to-diabetes wording is an absolute claim that exceeds the title's blood-sugar support framing.
bottleneck: The claim strength sits in a single red box while the picture shows only an ordinary drink of water.
action: Hypothesis: Change TO DIABETES to a softer phrase naming blood-sugar support, and compare click-through language against the current absolute wording.
counterexample: Seq 4 repeats the identical yellow, white and red-bar layout with an older man and a fruit bowl, showing the format is reused across channels.
hero_object: glass of water held to lips
medical_notes: The thumbnail says to say goodbye to diabetes by drinking water, which goes beyond the title wording about supporting blood sugar, and it shows no doctor credential.
